scenes.description: The 'Gobble gobble gobble' chant recurs three times and shifts owner/meaning: first as the turkeys' triumphant chaos, then as Tom's disguised battle-gobble, and finally as the kids' victory cry. Each instance wants a different color — menacing/overwhelming at first, sly and rallying in the middle, jubilant at the end — so the repetition lands as a running gag paying off.

Fancy technical turkey-anatomy words (caruncles, wattles, snoods) are applied to the silly flapping birds, the incongruity of elevated vocabulary for absurd creatures. Deliver these with mock-scientific relish; the callback at tt-045 ('fluffs snoods') should wink back at the earlier catalog.

Tom's favorite hiding spot/nest near the lunchroom is introduced casually as his private refuge, then becomes the emotional turning point when the turkeys invade his 'favorite nook.' The early mentions should feel cozy and low-stakes; the invasion at tt-037 is where Tom's fun collapses into panic — narrate the reversal with real alarm.

The school subjects Tom disrupts (Math, Reading, Music, Art) are echoed later as the very rooms/subjects the turkeys destroy (Art trampled, Music's drums flat, Math tests crumpled, Science blown apart). This mirror shows Tom's mischief boomeranging into real damage; the destruction lines should register as consequence, not more fun.

Tom's arc from 'Terrible Tom' the prankster to 'Turkey Tom' the protector of the school. The opening establishes him as a disruptive jokester; the ending recasts him as the school's fiercest defender, capped by the 'turkeys are finally cooked' pun. Narrate the opening with cheeky pride and the closing with earned, warm triumph.
